title: App network access
status.on: Active: lord-netperm enforces the rules in the kernel. Domain names: {dns}.
status.noDaemon: The lord-netperm service is not running: rules are saved but not enforced.
status.noBpf: lord-netperm could not use BPF on this computer ({error}): rules are saved but not enforced.
dns.packet: from the answers of the system DNS servers
dns.none: no source (domain rules do not apply)
mode.silentHint: Everything without a rule is allowed and each new connection is recorded in Monitor.
mode.offHint: Only explicit deny rules and restricted apps apply.
trustedHint: They use the network without recording their connections. A rule that denies something still applies.
restrictedHint: What you check is always denied to the app, above any rule or permission.
noMoreApps: All apps are already in a list.
footer: Rules apply to apps opened from LordOS (each one runs in its own scope). The owner of the computer decides them and they are kept in ~/.config/lordos/firewall.json.
desktopAlways: The desktop itself always has access to files, removable drives, the clipboard and Bluetooth; restrict individual apps instead.
linuxWhen: Applies immediately to the running app. Access to your files applies the next time it starts; for the microphone, the camera, USB and Bluetooth, restart the app so it can't get around them.
help.no-internet: only the local network; checked on every new connection.
help.no-lan: nothing on the local network, including this computer.
help.no-network: the app can't even open a network socket.
help.no-incoming: the app can't listen for connections.
help.no-camera: cameras can't be opened, directly or through the sound and video server.
help.no-mic: the app sees no microphone and its recordings are stopped.
help.no-screen: the app can't copy the screen; Linux apps never can.
help.no-usb: no raw USB devices, security keys or USB serial ports.
help.no-bluetooth: no Bluetooth sockets of its own.
help.no-files: only its own settings folders and the file you open it with.
help.no-clipboard: it can't read what you copied (LordOS apps).
mode.denyHint: Only what a rule allows can connect, and every denied connection is recorded in Monitor. This computer's own services (loopback) stay allowed.
lists.title: Blocklists
lists.summary: {lists} lists on, {entries} entries. LordOS downloads the lists you turn on once a day.
lists.customHint: A list you add is downloaded over HTTPS, checked line by line and used like the others. Only https addresses are accepted.
lists.footer: A list never overrides a rule you wrote for a domain or an address: allow it in Monitor → Network and it stays allowed. Names come from the system resolver: an app with its own encrypted DNS is checked by address only. An address that a listed name shares with a name that isn't listed stays allowed.
lists.err.cert: the server's certificate is not valid
lists.err.http: the server's answer was not valid
